description: We are a team of passionate and curious innovators participating in the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, working on “Abandoned but not Forgotten: Storytelling about NASA's Discarded Equipment on Moon and Mars." We are interested in space science, physics, data analysis, and innovative solutions to real-world challenges. Our goal is to explore microgravity combustion data and develop intelligent insights that can contribute to safer space missions.
summary:
Abandoned But Not Forgotten is an educational and cinematic video project that explores the legacy of inactive spacecraft, landers, rovers, and scientific instruments left behind on the Moon, Mars, and beyond. Through immersive visual storytelling and informative narration, the project brings attention to the machines that once operated on distant worlds and continue to represent significant milestones in space exploration.

The project presents the history, purpose, scientific contributions, and final resting places of these robotic explorers, explaining why certain hardware remains on extraterrestrial surfaces after missions conclude. By transforming scientific and mission-related information into an engaging documentary experience, it makes complex aspects of space exploration accessible to a broader audience.

The project addresses the challenge of communicating space science in an engaging and meaningful way. It encourages viewers to look beyond the active missions and recognize the historical, scientific, and technological value of spacecraft that have completed their journeys. Ultimately, it aims to inspire curiosity, promote space science awareness, and preserve the stories of humanity’s explorers—because the end of a mission does not mean the end of its legacy.

Project Description

Humanity’s pursuit of space exploration has left behind more than scientific discoveries. It has left a remarkable legacy of machines that ventured into environments beyond Earth. From lunar landing stages and scientific instruments on the Moon to retired robotic explorers and landers on Mars, these remnants represent the enduring achievements of our exploration of the Solar System.

“Abandoned but not forgotten” is an educational and cinematic documentary project dedicated to uncovering the stories of these inactive spacecraft and exploration systems. The project examines the missions, technologies, scientific contributions, and final resting places of space hardware that has completed its operational journey. It explores what remains on extraterrestrial surfaces, why these objects were left behind, and how they continue to hold scientific, historical, and cultural significance.

During the project we have discovered previous NASA’s Moon& Mars previous mission that was discarded after the project

1.     Ranger Program (1966-1968)

2.     Surveyor Mission (1966-1968)

3.     Apollo Lunar Mission (1969-1972)

4.     Lunar Roving Vehicles

5.     ALSEP Scientific Program

6.     Surveyor Landers

7.     Viking 1&2 Landers(1976)

8.     Mars Pathfinder & Sojourner(1997)

9.     Spirit & Opportunity(2004)

10.  Phoenix Lander(2008)

11.  Insight Lander(2018)

12.  Curiosity Rover(2012-Present)

13.  Preservance Rover & Ingenuity Helicopter(2021-Present/2024)

14.  Dawn Spacecraft(2007-2018)

15.  NEAR Shoemaker(1996-2001)

16.  Pioneer 10 &11(1972/1973)

17.  Voyager 1& 2(1977)

18.  Kepler Space Telescope (2009-2018)

For the data gathering we used NASA website, and for the collection of the mission's pictures, we used Wikipedia and NASA's previous data. For Masscot's design and animations, we used Canva. For dubbing and motion, we used Codex and Chatgpt.

In this project people can learn about the discoveries of these missions and how they were discarded after the project. Through immersive visual storytelling, informative narration, and an engaging documentary style presentation, the project transforms the concept of abandoned space hardware into a compelling exploration of human ingenuity and discovery. By revisiting these forgotten explorers, it seeks to deepen public understanding of space missions, inspire interest in planetary science, and emphasize the importance of preserving humanity’s technological heritage beyond Earth.

The project ultimately highlights a powerful idea “The end of a spacecraft’s mission does not mark the end of its contribution to science or humanity’s story of exploration”.
